Hi Avery,

Thanks for taking this. Attached is the completed SIG/CAIQ spreadsheet for the services you currently host for us (acme environment ids in column A). We are starting internal planning for our ISO 27001 certification and want to understand how Redwood's FedRAMP readiness roadmap might affect our timeline. High level asks: 

- Can you confirm the current evidence owners for encryption-in-transit, key management, and logging retention?
- Do you anticipate any boundary changes if we ask for FedRAMP-equivalent controls scoped to our environment?
- We have a planned external audit window in March 2027 — what lead time do you need for evidence samples and dry run?

Attached: acme_SIG_CAIQ_2026.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1.2MB).

Looking forward to a short intake call to align owners.

Lina — thanks for the SIG/CAIQ and the clear asks. Quick replies and proposed next steps below.

Short answers:
- Evidence owners: encryption-in-transit (infra-team / Kimberly), KMS rotations & access (security-ops / Grace), logging retention & extraction (platform-observability / Avery).
- Boundary changes: we have two flavors of deployment: hosted (shared control plane) and dedicated (customer VPC). If you stay on dedicated capacity we can keep your service boundary tight; FedRAMP-equivalent scoping usually requires additional attestation for control plane pieces — I'll let Kimberly outline impact below.
- Lead time for March 2027 external audit: recommend a dry run in late Jan 2027 and evidence sampling window in Feb 2027. That gives ~6 weeks to triage any gaps.

Immediate asks from us:
1) Can you confirm whether Acme is on Dedicated vs Hosted? (affects evidence sampling location)
2) Any regulatory constraints (data residency, PII scope) beyond the SIG?
3) Please share the FedRAMP scope notes if you have a draft — we can mark known gaps.

I've cc'd Kimberly and Grace to own the technical follow-ups. Can we do a 30-min intake call Thursday 10/22 9am PT?

Best,
Avery

Avery / Lina — copying in a short tech-readout.

On Tue, Oct 20, 2026 at 10:12 AM Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Lina — thanks for the SIG/CAIQ and the clear asks. Quick replies and proposed next steps below.

Notes from infra/security POV:
- If Acme is on Dedicated: evidence for in-transit encryption and KMS usage is scoped to the tenant VPC + assigned GPU instances. Minimal boundary change.
- If Acme is on Hosted: FedRAMP-equivalent scoping will require either (a) proof of logical separation + additional monitoring probes, or (b) a migration to Dedicated for the control plane pieces. We need to know which is acceptable to Acme.
- For KMS: we rotate customer-wrapped keys quarterly; KMS access logs are retained 12 months by default (can extend but subject to cost/retention SLA).
- Logging retention: standard retention windows are 90 days hot, archived for 18 months. For audit sampling we can produce snapshots (redacted) and extraction scripts.

Action items I can own:
- Prepare a short one-pager: "Redwood evidence map (encryption, KMS, logs)" — delivery by 10/27.
- Draft recommended intake for Acme: list of control artifacts we will need (SAML configs, key rotation policy, log extraction query templates).

Attachments referenced: fedramp_scope_notes_v1.pdf (stub).

—
Kimberly Park
